svg.title: Three primitives, each headed by the party that decides to reach for it
svg.desc: Three columns of identical width. Each is headed by a silhouette of the deciding party, a diamond for the model, a window for the application, and a person for the user, with the specification's own word beneath it in a chip: model-controlled, application-driven, and user-controlled. An arrow runs down from each actor into a box naming the primitive it starts and the method that carries it, tools through tools slash call, resources through resources slash read, and prompts through prompts slash get, each with a short gloss. A band across the bottom says the same data can legitimately be all three, that the question is never what the data is but who should decide to fetch it, and that each column names who may start an interaction and never who may stop one, because whoever starts it the host can still refuse.
svg.text: Three primitives, and who pulls each trigger
The wording under each figure is the specification's own. Only the actor differs.
Read from a name, a description,
and an input schema. Nothing in
attaches context by its own rule,
or because a user picked it
picks it from a menu, or types
The same data can legitimately be all three.
The question is never what the data is. It is who should decide to fetch it.
Each column names who may start an interaction, never who may stop one. Whoever starts it, the host can still refuse.
